title: Tria capita ex opere quodam majori inedito de theoria lunae

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the posthumous lunar-theory fragment E838, in the chapter on the apparent diameters and true hourly motions of sun and moon for eclipses. Notation: η is the mean elongation of moon from sun; v is the moon's eccentric anomaly; V is the sun's anomaly; k and e are the eccentricities of moon and sun; n is the ratio of the sun's mean motion to the moon's.

§8. On the previous page Euler had full trigonometric series for the moon's geocentric apparent diameter and its horizontal parallax. Here he specialises them to the eclipse configurations.
- Conjunction, η=0: cos η = cos 2η = 1, cos(2η−v) = cos v, cos(2η−2v) = cos 2v.
- Opposition, η=180°: the only change is that cos η = −1.
- Quadratures, η=90°: cos 2η = −1, cos(2η−v) = −cos v, cos(2η−2v) = −cos 2v, and the cos(2η±V) terms turn into cos V terms.

Resulting values. Diameter at conjunction:
- constant: 31'17'' + 14.1'' − 0.6'' = 31'30.5''
- cos v coefficient: −102.4 − 19.9 = −122.3''
- cos 2v coefficient: 2.8 + 1.4 = 4.2''

At opposition the constant is 31'32''. At quadrature the diameter is 31'3'' − 82.5 cos v + 1.4 cos 2v + (0.2 + 0.4 + 0.4) cos V. The parallax is treated the same way, using the previous page's 56'44'', −185.7, 5.1, 25.5, −1.0, 2.6, −36.1 and 0.4/0.7/0.9.

Apogee (v=0) and perigee (v=180°) values: 29'32''/33'36'', 53'34''/60'58'', 29'34''/33'38'', 53'36''/61'0'', 29'41''/32'27'', 53'50''/58'50''. Euler notes that for eclipses only the dependence on the moon's eccentric anomaly matters; the solar-anomaly terms are negligible.

§9. He begins the true hourly motion of the moon. He starts from the perturbed area law
 dφ = (α − (3/2) n² M) · c²/z² · du,
where u is the mean anomaly with du = dv(1 + k cos v), and z/c is the distance in units of the mean distance. Here the factor α − (3/2) n² M encodes the solar torque, i.e. the departure from Kepler's second law. The constants are:
- α = 1.0070234 (log 0.0030396)
- log((3/2) n²) = 7.9312851−10, giving n ≈ 0.0754, the ratio of the anomalistic month to the year
- du = 32'39''48''' per hour, the mean anomalistic hourly motion (360°/27.5546 d)

The earlier series for M (terms in cos 2η, cos(2η±v), cos 2(η−v), cos(2η±V), cos(2η−v±V), cos η, cos 3η, cos(η−v), cos 4η, cos v) is recalled.

§10. The numerical numerator α − (3/2) n² M is tabulated, with log10 coefficients printed beneath each term: 0.004662 cos 2η, 0.0011281 cos(2η−v), 0.0001987 cos v, and so on. On the next page it is multiplied by (c/z)², with c/z given as its own series, to give dφ/du as a Fourier series in v, V and η.
errors: Perigee diameter at conjunction: the unrounded coefficients give 1890.5 + 122.3 + 4.2 = 2017'' = 33'37''. Euler prints 33'36'' because he works from the rounded 31'30'', 122 and 4. This is a rounding discrepancy only.

In the quadrature formulas the dropped terms 0.3 cos(v−V) and 0.6 cos(v−V) are, in fact, nearly cancelled by the (2η−v±V) terms (which become −cos(v−V) at η=90°). So the omission is justified, though not stated.

Sign ambiguity versus the next page. The printed sign before 0.0000364 cos(2η−v−V) appears as '+' or '=' in the scan. The next page's abbreviation writes −G cos(2η−v−V). Either the sign here or the shorthand there is inconsistent; this cannot be settled from this page alone.
Notation clash, not a mathematical error: Euler uses the letter M both for the whole perturbation function and for the coefficient Mε of cos η.

ideas.what: Specialisation of the series for lunar apparent diameter and horizontal parallax to syzygies and quadratures, with apogee/perigee extremes, for eclipse computation
ideas.modern_name: Lunar parallax/semidiameter tables including evection and variation contributions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in 18th-century lunar tables (Mayer, Euler, Clairaut)
ideas.where_published: Euler's lunar theories E187 (1753) and E418 (1772) contain parallax series. This specific syzygy/quadrature tabulation is only known to me from this posthumous fragment.

ideas.what: True hourly motion from the perturbed area law dφ = (α − (3/2)n²M) c²/z² du
ideas.modern_name: Angular-momentum (area) integral modified by solar perturbing torque; lunar velocity series
ideas.usually_credited_to: Newton/Clairaut/Euler; the area-law perturbation approach is in Euler's lunar theories
ideas.where_published: Euler, Theoria motuum lunae (E418, 1772), and earlier E187

ideas.what: Use of an anomalistic hourly motion du = 32'39''48''' with v the eccentric anomaly, and n taken relative to the anomalistic month

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine numerical specialisation of lunar diameter and parallax series and sets up the hourly-motion computation. I checked the arithmetic and it is correct to the stated rounding. Nothing here is conceptually new relative to Euler's published lunar theories.
transcription_corrections: 'lunarinm' is a printing typo in the original for 'lunarium'.
The sign before 0.0000364 cos(2η−v−V) is unclear in the scan ('+' versus '=', possibly '−'). The next page uses −G, so '+[?]' should be flagged as uncertain.
The fourth-row leading sign before 0.0000139 cos 3η appears as '+' in the image. This is consistent with +K cos 3η on the next page.
The log values under each coefficient are base-10 logarithms with the −10 characteristic; e.g. 7.66857 = log 0.004662.
